def solution(items):
    # Infer from provided examples:
    # Returns 1 if there exists a pair of elements with sum zero? Check:
    # [-1,0,1] -> 1 (has -1 and 1)
    # [1,2,3] -> 0 (no pair summing to 0)
    # [1,1] -> 0 (no opposite)
    # [0] -> 1 (single zero)
    # [2,1] -> 0
    # [1] -> 0
    # [5,-5,5] -> 0 (has 5 and -5, but maybe only count unique pairs? unclear)
    # [] -> 0
    # [3,2,1] -> 0
    # [1,-10,10,0,-2] -> 1 (has -10 and 10 or 0? multiple possibilities)
    #
    # Hypothesis: return 1 if there exists at least one zero OR there exists a pair (a,b) with a == -b but only if zero included? 
    # Check: [-1,0,1] -> 1 (has pair and zero)
    # [0] -> 1 (zero)
    # [5,-5,5] -> 0 would violate zero-pair rule because there exists 5 and -5; but expected 0.
    # So maybe count of zeroes? Not: [-1,0,1] has zero and nonzero count -> 1
    # [1,-10,10,0,-2] -> 1 (has 10 and -10 or zero)
    # [5,-5,5] -> 0 despite pair
    # Perhaps rule: return 1 if exactly one zero? [0] ->1; [ -1,0,1 ] ->1; [1,-10,10,0,-2] has zero ->1; but [5,-5,5] has no zero ->0
    # Then condition is presence of zero in list.
    # Check: [] ->0, [1] ->0, [2,1] ->0, [3,2,1]->0, [1,1]->0, [5,-5,5]->0
    # All align with "return 1 if 0 is in items else 0".
    return 1 if 0 in items else 0
```
